ours-gaming.short: Night School's specification-gaming runs, trained for this film
ours-gaming.citation: media/school/gaming/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_gaming.mjs from system/school/gaming.mjs: REINFORCE on the attention model from its step-200 checkpoint and from the trained model, against four checkers (gamed, patched, fixed, exact), 800 steps, batch 32, three seeds each; correctness judged against the generator's exact answer.
claims: From step 200: gamed checker reward 0.313 to 0.997, correctness to 0 (peaks 0.74 to 0.99 first); first word right 0.982, answers never stop.
Patched: correctness 0.938 (one seed 0.832); fixed: 0.984; correlation of reward and correctness 0.998 (fixed) against -0.384 (gamed).
From the trained model the gamed checker is not exploited: correctness 0.999.
From the trained model the patched checker let one of three runs drift into padding: correctness 0.918, 0.543, 1.0 (start 0.965).
ours-gaming.does_not_prove: Anything about large models; one task, one optimiser, one learning rate.

krakovna2020.short: Krakovna and others 2020, Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity
krakovna2020.citation: Krakovna, V., Uesato, J., Mikulik, V., Rahtz, M., Everitt, T., Kumar, R., Kenton, Z., Leike, J., Legg, S. (2020). Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity. DeepMind blog, 21 April 2020, with the specification gaming examples list.
krakovna2020.read: to be read by the fact-check
claims: Specification gaming is behaviour that satisfies the literal specification of an objective without achieving the intended outcome; the post collects many examples.

baker2025.short: Baker and others 2025, Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
baker2025.citation: Baker, B., Huizinga, J., Gao, L., Dou, Z., Guan, M. Y., Madry, A., Zaremba, W., Pachocki, J., Farhi, D. (2025). Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation. arXiv:2503.11926.
baker2025.read: to be read by the fact-check
claims: A monitor reading chain-of-thought catches reward hacking in agentic coding environments; putting the monitor into the training reward leads to obfuscated reward hacking.
